sensory_notes.look: Pourable and evenly coloured, with no dry flour caught at the bottom of the bowl and no lumps riding up on the spoon.
sensory_notes.sound: The spoon moves freely with a soft slosh; none of the dry scrape of unwetted flour against the bowl.
sensory_notes.smell: Plain and milky, faintly of raw flour.

sensory_notes.look: Fully liquid and still pale yellow, with a fine foam of small bubbles covering the surface and no brown flecks settling at the bottom of the pan.
sensory_notes.sound: A steady fine sizzle as the water in the butter cooks off; it quietens as the foam thins.
sensory_notes.smell: Warm and creamy, with nothing nutty or toasted about it yet.

sensory_notes.look: Pale, smooth, and visibly lightened, spreading against the bowl with no firm lumps left and no shine of melted fat.
sensory_notes.sound: A soft slapping against the side of the bowl rather than the hard scrape of cold butter.
sensory_notes.smell: Faintly sweet and milky, no more than that.

sensory_notes.look: Cold through and a little thicker than it was warm, pouring in a smooth stream, the surface unbroken with no skin on top.
sensory_notes.sound: A soft heavy pour, with no steam or ticking left in the bowl.
sensory_notes.smell: Faint — cold sweet milk and egg; the smell only comes forward as it warms in the mouth.

sensory_notes.look: An even opaque film clings to the back of the spoon instead of running off it, and a finger drawn through leaves a clean line that does not close up.
sensory_notes.sound: The stirring has gone quiet and heavy — the spoon meets resistance where it used to move freely.
sensory_notes.smell: Warm sweet milk and egg, with nothing scorched about it.

sensory_notes.look: Grainy — fine specks and threads of set egg suspended in a thin watery liquid that has lost both its gloss and its body.
sensory_notes.sound: The drag on the spoon slackens off again after having thickened; it sloshes rather than pours.
sensory_notes.smell: Faintly of scrambled egg, sometimes with a scorched edge underneath.

sensory_notes.look: Doubled and domed, holding a dent for a moment when pressed with a fingertip rather than springing straight back.
sensory_notes.sound: Deflates with a soft exhale when you press it down.
sensory_notes.smell: Yeasty and slightly winey, stronger than after the first rise.

sensory_notes.look: The surface has gone from ragged and patchy to smooth and faintly satiny; it stretches without tearing and pulls back when released.
sensory_notes.sound: A soft slap on the board with each fold, no tacky sticking as you turn it.
sensory_notes.smell: Warm, yeasty, and clean.

sensory_notes.look: Gathered into one mass that pulls away from the sides of the bowl, matte rather than wet-shiny, soft but no longer smearing on your fingers.
sensory_notes.sound: Comes away from the bowl cleanly, without the sticky suck of a wet dough.
sensory_notes.smell: Yeasty and faintly sweet from the milk and sugar.

sensory_notes.look: Gathers into one mass and pulls away from the bowl, matte rather than wet-shiny, holding the shape of your hand when pressed.
sensory_notes.sound: Lifts away silently — no sticky suck against the bowl.
sensory_notes.smell: Sweet and warm with the cinnamon and nutmeg coming forward.

sensory_notes.look: Comes quickly to the top of the fat within a few seconds and floats there, visibly puffed and swelling at the edges.
sensory_notes.sound: An immediate steady ring of bubbling around each one.
sensory_notes.smell: Sweet frying dough and warm spice.

sensory_notes.look: White, dense, and still glossy; a peak pulled up by the beater stands without folding over, and the mass stays where it is when the bowl is tipped.
sensory_notes.sound: The beater works through a heavy foam with a dull whisper instead of splashing through liquid.
sensory_notes.smell: Almost nothing — clean and neutral; a sulphurous note means the eggs are old.

sensory_notes.look: Pale yellow, foamed and thickened, falling from the beater in a wide ribbon that sits on the surface a moment before sinking.
sensory_notes.sound: The beater moves through with an airy swish instead of the slosh of raw egg.
sensory_notes.smell: Clean and barely eggy.

sensory_notes.look: Yolks broken up and evenly gold with no lighter streaks left, still thick and liquid, the surface flat with no foam or bubbles on it.
sensory_notes.sound: A quiet heavy drag as the fork goes through — none of the airy swish of eggs being beaten light.
sensory_notes.smell: Plainly eggy, unchanged from raw.

sensory_notes.look: The surface shimmers and moves faintly with no smoke rising; a one-inch cube of bread dropped in browns in about a minute.
sensory_notes.sound: A lively steady sizzle the instant dough touches it — silence means too cold, a violent spitting crackle means too hot.
sensory_notes.smell: Clean and hot, with nothing acrid or scorched about it.

sensory_notes.look: An even brown across the submerged face, with a paler band left around the middle where the doughnut sat at the fat line.
sensory_notes.sound: The bubbling slows and quiets as the moisture cooks out.
sensory_notes.smell: Toasted and sweet with the spice, well short of anything scorched.

sensory_notes.look: Steam lifting off the surface and a ring of small bubbles around the edge of the pan, with no rolling boil in the middle; a thin skin may start to form.
sensory_notes.sound: A faint ticking against the pan bottom — no churning or bubbling up the sides.
sensory_notes.smell: Warm and faintly sweet, like cooked milk; any hint of scorch means it has caught and should be started again.

sensory_notes.look: No steam rising from the surface; the melted butter sits as a thin unbroken film rather than re-hardening into flecks.
sensory_notes.sound: Silent — nothing ticking or settling in the pan.
sensory_notes.smell: Mildly milky and sweet, no longer sharp with heat.

sensory_notes.look: An oven thermometer steady at 400–425°F (205–220°C); a pinch of flour thrown on the oven floor browns within about a minute.
sensory_notes.sound: The element or burner cycling off rather than running continuously.
sensory_notes.smell: Clean and dry, with nothing burning off the racks.

sensory_notes.look: Tops a deep even gold, the sides where the rolls nearly touch a paler gold, the parted crease showing a lighter seam.
sensory_notes.sound: A hollow knock when a roll is lifted and tapped underneath.
sensory_notes.smell: Toasted bread and warm butter, well short of anything scorched.

sensory_notes.look: Visibly puffed and softened, the fold opened a little way along the crease — a slight parting, not a flop wide open — and dough that fills back slowly when pressed.
sensory_notes.sound: Silent; nothing to hear at this stage.
sensory_notes.smell: Yeasty with a butter note from the brushed halves.

sensory_notes.look: One smooth pale paste, no dry flour visible anywhere and no grainy patches at the edge of the pan; it holds together on the spoon rather than falling apart.
sensory_notes.sound: A quiet even sizzle, softer than the bare butter made a moment before.
sensory_notes.smell: Faintly toasty, like warm biscuit dough, with no scorched edge to it.

sensory_notes.look: Even and lump-free with a satin shine, coating the back of a spoon in a thin translucent film that runs off rather than clinging thickly.
sensory_notes.sound: A gentle bubbling around the edge of the pan and a smooth even sweep of the spoon with no lumps knocking against it.
sensory_notes.smell: Sweet warm milk and butter, with the raw-flour smell gone.

sensory_notes.look: One uniform, slightly thickened liquid — no pale streaks of unmixed milk and no lumps of paste riding on the spoon — before the next addition goes in.
sensory_notes.sound: The stirring loosens off: the drag of the paste gives way to a fluid slosh as each addition goes through.
sensory_notes.smell: Warm milk over a faint scent of raw flour.

sensory_notes.look: Glossy and uniform with no dry streaks of flour, pulling off the spoon in a sheet rather than dropping in lumps.
sensory_notes.sound: A heavy rhythmic slap against the side of the bowl as the batter thickens and grabs the spoon.
sensory_notes.smell: Sweet and yeasty, with the warm milk still coming through.

sensory_notes.look: Roughly doubled and domed, the surface puffed with bubbles visible just under the skin.
sensory_notes.sound: A soft sigh as it settles when you first cut it down.
sensory_notes.smell: Yeasty with a faint sourness, like the inside of a bakery.

sensory_notes.look: An even brown across the raised pattern with paler wells between, edges crisp and set, and the waffle releasing from the grid without pulling or tearing.
sensory_notes.sound: The hiss of steam escaping at the seam has died down to almost nothing.
sensory_notes.smell: Toasted and buttery, well short of anything scorched.

sensory_notes.look: Both faces dry and clean-looking with no smoke lifting off them; a drop of water flicked onto the pattern skitters and vanishes at once instead of sitting and steaming, and fat brushed on runs thin and clear rather than pooling.
sensory_notes.sound: A sharp immediate hiss the moment fat or batter meets the grid — silence means the iron has gone cold.
sensory_notes.smell: Hot metal and just-melted fat, with nothing acrid or scorched about it.

sensory_notes.look: No streaks or islands of white left anywhere in the bowl, the batter visibly lighter and puffier than it was, holding a soft mound for a moment where the spoon lifted out.
sensory_notes.sound: Quiet — a soft cutting stroke through the batter, with none of the slap of beating.
sensory_notes.smell: Milky and faintly eggy.

sensory_notes.look: The cake broken up completely, the water clouded a milky tan with no grains or lumps left on the bottom.
sensory_notes.sound: Nothing — the spoon moves through it freely, with no grit against the bowl.
sensory_notes.smell: Distinctly yeasty and bready, faintly beery.

sensory_notes.look: Glossy sauce clinging to every strand; no white curds, no watery puddle collecting at the bottom of the pan.
sensory_notes.sound: A soft slip as you toss — nothing sticks or squeaks.
sensory_notes.smell: Cheese and pork fat, no sulfurous cooked-egg edge.

sensory_notes.look: The outer edge of each kernel turns glassy while the center stays a chalky white dot.
sensory_notes.sound: Kernels click faintly against the pan when stirred — drier than they went in.

sensory_notes.look: Shake the pan: loose rice rolls in a wave across it. When the wave stops rolling and the rice starts sticking to itself, it has drunk that addition.
sensory_notes.sound: The wet slosh dries out to a heavier, tackier shuffle.

sensory_notes.look: After the rest, the risotto is a single glossy body — it spreads on a tilted plate in a slow wave rather than standing in a mound.
A toothpick pushed to the center comes out with no wet batter — dry, or carrying a few moist crumbs at most.
The crust is an even brown and the edges have shrunk back from the sides of the pan, leaving a visible gap.
sensory_notes.smell: Deep banana and caramel — the sugars at the edge have browned.
